newsitem.title: USA: Intel says to resume comments to analysts.
newsitem.headline: Intel says to resume comments to analysts.

text.p: Intel Corp said it plans to resume giving Wall Street analysts help in forecasting its financial results after Proposition 211 was rejected by California voters.
"We will move into a mode of resuming our normal kinds of communication activity" with analysts and investors, said company spokesman Howard High.

Last month, Intel, the world's biggest maker of computer chips, stopped helping analysts come up with earnings forecasts because of Proposition 211, a measure that would have made it easier for investors to sue a company for sharp stock declines.
Technology companies, which usually have more volatile stocks, have been a favorite target of shareholder class-action lawsuits.
When Intel released its third-quarter earnings last month, the company said it would not make any more statements about upcoming quarters to avoid exposing itself to litigation.
Intel shares and other technology stocks rose sharply following Prop. 211's defeat. In midafternoon trading, Intel was up 2-3/8 at 116-3/8.
